records.source: יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ מָלַ֗ךְ בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָתֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ אֲבִיָּ֖ה בַּת־זְכַרְיָֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: Hezekiah reigned, a son of twenty and five year[s], and twenty and nine year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem; and [the] name of his mother [was] Abijah daughter of Zechariah.
pieces: Hezekiah became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.

L.1: Hezekiah became king [as] a son of twenty-five years, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother [was] Abijah daughter of Zechariah.

R.1: Hezekiah became king at the age of twenty-five, and he ruled for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.

decisions.choice: a retelling of 2 Kings 18:1-2, with three differences
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 18:1-2 dates Hezekiah's accession by the third year of Hoshea king of Israel; Chronicles leaves that date out, as it leaves out most dates tied to the northern kings. Chronicles spells the king's name in its longer form throughout, and it names his mother Abijah where 2 Kings 18:2 has the short form Abi. The rest of the verse is the same.

decisions.choice: a son of twenty-five years: twenty-five years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years, as in 2 Kings 18:2.

decisions.choice: his mother: the queen mother named in the formula
decisions.reason: For each king of Judah the formula names his mother, who held a place of honor at court (1 Kings 15:13). Abijah means "my father is Yahweh".

decisions.choice: the wording of 2 Kings 18:2, with the name first
decisions.reason: The Hebrew opens with the king's name, so each level begins "Hezekiah became king" and then keeps the wording used in 2 Kings 18:2 and in the accession formula throughout these books.

records.heading: Hezekiah cleanses the temple

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה דָּוִ֥יד אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he did the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh, according to all that had done David his father.
pieces: He did what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in every way as his ancestor David had done.

L.2: And he did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to all that David his father had done.

R.2: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right, in every way, just as his ancestor David had done.

decisions.choice: the same verdict as 2 Kings 18:3, word for word
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is the same as 2 Kings 18:3, and the wording is kept. Kings goes on to say that Hezekiah removed the high places (2 Kings 18:4); Chronicles turns first to the temple and tells of the high places later (31:1).

decisions.choice: did what was right in Yahweh's eyes: the good verdict, without any reservation
decisions.reason: Hezekiah is measured against David "according to all" he did, the highest praise the formula gives. Chronicles gives four chapters (29-32) to show what that meant.

decisions.choice: David his father: his ancestor David
decisions.reason: David lived some three hundred years before Hezekiah. "Father" also means a forefather, as in 2 Kings 18:3.

decisions.choice: did the right in [the] eyes of / did what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the good verdict at each level throughout these books.

decisions.choice: his ancestor David
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestor" for "father" wherever David is called the father of a later king, as 2 Kings 18:3 does; Literal keeps "father".

records.source: ה֣וּא בַשָּׁנָה֩ הָרִאשׁוֹנָ֨ה לְמָלְכ֜וֹ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן פָּתַ֛ח אֶת־דַּלְת֥וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה וַֽיְחַזְּקֵֽם׃
records.gloss: He, in the year the first of his reigning, in the month the first, opened [the] doors of [the] house of Yahweh and strengthened them.
pieces: In his first year as king, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and made them strong again.

L.3: He, in the first year of his reign, in the first month, opened the doors of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and repaired them.

R.3: In the first month of the first year that he was king, Hezekiah opened the doors of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and repaired them.

decisions.choice: He: Hezekiah himself, set first for emphasis
decisions.reason: The verse begins with the pronoun, which Hebrew does not need. It puts Hezekiah in the foreground and sets what he did against what his father Ahaz had done: Ahaz had shut the doors of the house of Yahweh (28:24).

decisions.choice: in the first month: the first month of the year, in spring
decisions.reason: The first month of Israel's year (Exodus 12:2) was the month of the Passover. The phrase most likely means the first month of the calendar in Hezekiah's first year, not the first month after he took the throne. The cleansing took until the sixteenth day of this month (verse 17), past the day of the Passover, which is why the Passover was kept in the second month (30:2-3).

decisions.choice: strengthened them: repaired them
decisions.reason: The verb means to make strong. Used of buildings it means to repair (24:5, 12). Ahaz had stripped the temple (28:24; 2 Kings 16:17-18), and later Hezekiah himself took the gold from these doors to pay Assyria (2 Kings 18:16).

decisions.choice: made them strong again (Balanced); Hezekiah ... the LORD's temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the verb, "make strong", with "again" for the repair of what Ahaz had damaged. Readable names Hezekiah for "he" and says "temple" for "house of the LORD", as Readable does in these books.

records.source: וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת־הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְאֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֑ם וַיַּֽאַסְפֵ֖ם לִרְח֥וֹב הַמִּזְרָֽח׃
records.gloss: And he brought the priests and the Levites and gathered them to [the] square of the east.
pieces: He brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them in the open square on the east side.

L.4: And he brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them in the square of the east.

R.4: He brought together the priests and the Levites in the open square on the east side of the temple.

decisions.choice: the priests and the Levites: the two ranks of temple servants
decisions.reason: The priests were the descendants of Aaron, who served at the altar and inside the sanctuary. The other Levites helped them, kept the gates, carried, cleaned and led the singing (1 Chronicles 23:27-32). Both ranks are called here, and the work in verses 16-17 is shared between them.

decisions.choice: the square of the east: an open space east of the temple
alternatives: a square on the east side of the city
decisions.reason: The temple faced east, so this was most likely the open ground in front of its entrance (compare Ezra 10:9, "the square of the house of God"). It may instead be a square on the east side of the city.

decisions.choice: of the temple
decisions.reason: Readable names the temple as the place the square lay east of, which the Hebrew implies.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָהֶ֖ם שְׁמָע֣וּנִי הַלְוִיִּ֑ם עַתָּ֣ה הִֽתְקַדְּשׁ֗וּ וְקַדְּשׁוּ֙ אֶת־בֵּ֤ית יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֔ם וְהוֹצִ֥יאוּ אֶת־הַנִּדָּ֖ה מִן־הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, hear me, the Levites! Now consecrate yourselves, and consecrate [the] house of Yahweh, [the] God of your fathers, and bring out the impurity from the holy [place].
pieces: He said to them, "Listen to me, you Levites! Consecrate yourselves now. Then consecrate the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, and carry everything impure out of the holy place.

L.5: And he said to them, "Hear me, Levites! Now consecrate yourselves, and consecrate the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, and bring out the impurity from the holy place.

R.5: He said to them, "Listen to me, Levites! Make yourselves holy now, and make the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, holy too. Take everything that makes the holy place unclean, and carry it out.

decisions.choice: Levites: the whole tribe, priests included
decisions.reason: Hezekiah had called both priests and Levites (verse 4), and he speaks of duties that belonged to the priests alone, such as burning incense (verse 11; 26:18). Here "Levites" names the whole tribe of Levi, as it sometimes does (Deuteronomy 18:1).

decisions.choice: consecrate yourselves ... consecrate the house: two forms of one verb
decisions.reason: The first form means to make oneself holy: to wash, keep from what defiles and be ready for holy service (Exodus 19:22; 1 Chronicles 15:12). The second means to make something holy: to set the house apart again for God and make it fit for worship.

decisions.choice: the impurity: whatever defiled the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word is used of a woman's monthly impurity (Leviticus 15:19), and from there of anything that makes a person or place unclean and must be put away (Ezra 9:11; Lamentations 1:17). Here it means the idols, altars and refuse that had been brought in or left to lie while the temple was shut (28:24; 2 Kings 16:10-18).

decisions.choice: the holy place: the sanctuary as a whole
decisions.reason: The word can name the outer room of the temple, but here it stands for the whole sanctuary, as the work of verses 16-17 shows.

decisions.choice: the God of your ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers" when the word means forefathers, as 2 Chronicles 15:12 does; Literal keeps "fathers".

decisions.choice: make yourselves holy; make ... holy
decisions.reason: Readable says what "consecrate" means in plain words, as 1 Chronicles 15:12 does.

records.source: כִּֽי־מָעֲל֣וּ אֲבֹתֵ֗ינוּ וְעָשׂ֥וּ הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ וַיַּֽעַזְבֻ֑הוּ וַיַּסֵּ֧בּוּ פְנֵיהֶ֛ם מִמִּשְׁכַּ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה וַיִּתְּנוּ־עֹֽרֶף׃
records.gloss: For were unfaithful our fathers and did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh our God and forsook him, and turned their faces from [the] dwelling of Yahweh and gave [the] back of [the] neck.
pieces: Our fathers were unfaithful and did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. They forsook {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; they turned their faces from the place where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dwells and showed it their backs.

L.6: For our fathers acted unfaithfully and did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, and they forsook {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And they turned their faces away from the dwelling place of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and gave [it the] back of [the] neck.

R.6: Our fathers were not faithful to God. They did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God said was evil, and they left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They turned away from the place where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and turned their backs on it.

decisions.choice: were unfaithful: broke faith with God
decisions.reason: The verb means to break trust, to fail to give what is owed, often by taking what belongs to God or giving his worship to others. It is one of Chronicles' key words for sin (1 Chronicles 10:13; 2 Chronicles 26:16; 28:19, 22).

decisions.choice: our fathers: the generations just before, Ahaz's above all
decisions.reason: Hezekiah means the people of his father's day and before, who had seen the temple shut (28:22-25). Verse 9 speaks of these same fathers falling in battle.

decisions.choice: the dwelling: the temple as the place where Yahweh lives
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the tabernacle in the wilderness, the tent where God dwelt among his people (Exodus 25:9). Here it names the temple that had taken its place.

decisions.choice: gave the back of the neck: turned their backs in contempt
decisions.reason: To show someone the back of the neck is to turn away from them on purpose and refuse to look at them (Jeremiah 2:27; 32:33). It is the opposite of turning the face toward God in prayer.

decisions.choice: our fathers
decisions.reason: Here "fathers" is kept at every level, since Hezekiah means recent generations, people his hearers knew, rather than distant ancestors.

decisions.choice: showed it their backs (Balanced); turned their backs on it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plain gesture of turning one's back. Literal keeps "gave [it the] back of [the] neck".

records.source: גַּ֣ם סָֽגְר֞וּ דַּלְת֣וֹת הָאוּלָ֗ם וַיְכַבּוּ֙ אֶת־הַנֵּר֔וֹת וּקְטֹ֖רֶת לֹ֣א הִקְטִ֑ירוּ וְעֹלָה֙ לֹא־הֶעֱל֣וּ בַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ לֵאלֹהֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Also they shut [the] doors of the porch and put out the lamps, and incense not they burned, and burnt offering not they offered up in the holy [place] to [the] God of Israel.
pieces: They even shut the doors of the porch and put out the lamps. They did not burn incense or offer burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.

L.7: They also shut the doors of the porch and put out the lamps, and they did not burn incense, and they did not offer up burnt offering in the holy place to the God of Israel.

R.7: They even closed the doors of the temple porch and put out the lamps. They stopped burning incense and offering burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: they shut the doors of the porch: the closing of the temple under Ahaz
decisions.reason: Chronicles has already told how Ahaz shut the doors of the house of Yahweh and set up altars of his own all over Jerusalem (28:24-25). Hezekiah's first act undoes it (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the lamps, the incense, the burnt offering: the daily service
decisions.reason: The lamps were to burn every night, incense was burned morning and evening, and a burnt offering was made every morning and evening (Exodus 27:20-21; 29:38-42; 30:7-8; 2 Chronicles 13:11). Stopping them meant that the regular worship of Yahweh had ceased.

decisions.choice: temple porch
decisions.reason: Readable says which porch is meant, as 2 Chronicles 8:12 does.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ קֶ֣צֶף יְהוָ֔ה עַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּתְּנֵ֤ם לְזַֽעֲוָה֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה וְלִשְׁרֵקָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר אַתֶּ֥ם רֹאִ֖ים בְּעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And was [the] wrath of Yahweh on Judah and Jerusalem, and he made them into a terror, into a horror and into a hissing, as you [are] seeing with your eyes.
pieces: So the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came upon Judah and Jerusalem, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them an object of terror, horror and hissing, as you can see with your own eyes.

L.8: And the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them a terror, a horror and a hissing, as you are seeing with your eyes.

R.8: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became angry with Judah and Jerusalem. He made them a sight that fills people with fear and shock, so that they whistle at it in scorn. You can see this with your own eyes.

decisions.choice: a terror: the word read aloud
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text give a rare spelling of the word; the vowels and the margin give the usual form, the word used in Deuteronomy 28:25. The meaning is the same either way: something that makes those who see it tremble.

decisions.choice: a terror, a horror and a hissing: the language of the covenant curse
decisions.reason: These are the words of the curse Moses warned of (Deuteronomy 28:25, 37) and that the prophets used for what would come on Judah. The same words come together in Jeremiah 29:18 (compare Jeremiah 19:8; 25:9, 18). Hezekiah says the curse has already begun to fall.

decisions.choice: a hissing: the whistle people gave at a ruin
decisions.reason: Passers-by would whistle or hiss at the sight of a ruined place or people, in shock and scorn (1 Kings 9:8; Lamentations 2:15-16).

decisions.choice: a horror: a ruin that appalls those who see it
decisions.reason: The word joins the ideas of desolation and of the dismay it causes in those who see it.

decisions.choice: a sight that fills people with fear and shock, so that they whistle at it in scorn
decisions.reason: Readable explains the three words instead of listing them, and says what the hissing meant.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָפְל֥וּ אֲבוֹתֵ֖ינוּ בֶּחָ֑רֶב וּבָנֵ֨ינוּ וּבְנוֹתֵ֧ינוּ וְנָשֵׁ֛ינוּ בַּשְּׁבִ֖י עַל־זֹֽאת׃
records.gloss: And look, have fallen our fathers by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives [are] in captivity on this.
pieces: Because of this our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons, our daughters and our wives are in captivity.

L.9: And look, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives [are] in captivity because of this.

R.9: That is why our fathers were killed in battle and our sons, daughters and wives were taken away as prisoners.

decisions.choice: fallen by the sword ... in captivity: the defeats under Ahaz
decisions.reason: Under Ahaz, Aram and Israel killed many in Judah and carried off captives (28:5-8), though the captives taken to Samaria were sent back (28:9-15). The Edomites and Philistines also raided Judah and took prisoners (28:17-18). Some of those taken were still in captivity.

decisions.choice: because of this: because of the unfaithfulness of verses 6-7
decisions.reason: "This" points back to what the fathers did. The losses were the result of turning away from Yahweh, as verse 8 has said.

decisions.choice: Because of this ... (Balanced); That is why ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring "because of this" to the front, where it links the verse to what goes before, in place of the opening "look". Readable says "killed in battle" for "fallen by the sword".

records.source: עַתָּה֙ עִם־לְבָבִ֔י לִכְר֣וֹת בְּרִ֔ית לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְיָשֹׁ֥ב מִמֶּ֖נּוּ חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Now with my heart [it is] to cut a covenant with Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, and may turn from us [the] burning of his anger.
pieces: I have now set my heart on making a covenant with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, in the hope that the heat of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger will turn away from us.

L.10: Now [it is] with my heart to make a covenant with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, so that the burning of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger may turn away from us.

R.10: Now I have decided to make a covenant with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will no longer be angry with us.

decisions.choice: with my heart: I intend, I have resolved
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will. "It is with my heart" means that the speaker has made up his mind (1 Chronicles 22:7; 28:2).

decisions.choice: make a covenant: bind himself and the people by a solemn pledge
decisions.reason: Literally "cut a covenant", the usual Hebrew phrase. Here it is a pledge to return to Yahweh and keep faith with him, as under Asa and Jehoiada (15:12; 23:16).

decisions.choice: so that ... may turn away: the purpose and hope of the covenant
decisions.reason: The verb has the form of a wish. Hezekiah hopes that renewed loyalty will bring an end to the anger of verse 8.

decisions.choice: I have set my heart on (Balanced); I have decided; he will no longer be angry with us (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the heart in a common English phrase for a firm intention (m1); Readable says what the idioms of the heart and of burning anger mean.

records.source: בָּנַ֕י עַתָּ֖ה אַל־תִּשָּׁל֑וּ כִּֽי־בָכֶ֞ם בָּחַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לַעֲמֹ֤ד לְפָנָיו֙ לְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ וְלִהְי֥וֹת ל֖וֹ מְשָׁרְתִ֥ים וּמַקְטִרִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: My sons, now do not be negligent, for you has chosen Yahweh to stand before him to serve him, and to be for him ministers and burning incense.
pieces: My sons, do not be negligent now, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen you to stand before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ministers and to burn incense."

L.11: My sons, now do not be negligent, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen you to stand before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ministers and burners of incense."

R.11: My sons, do not be careless now. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen you to stand in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. You are to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants and burn incense to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: my sons: a warm address from one in authority
decisions.reason: Hezekiah was a young man (verse 1), and many of those he spoke to were older. "My sons" is the language of a leader or teacher who cares for those under him (1 Samuel 3:6; Proverbs 1:8).

decisions.choice: do not be negligent: do not hold back or grow slack
decisions.reason: The verb means to be at ease or careless. Hezekiah urges them not to delay or do the work half-heartedly.

decisions.choice: chosen to stand before him, to serve him and burn incense
decisions.reason: This is how the Law describes the tribe of Levi's calling (Deuteronomy 10:8; 18:5; 1 Chronicles 23:13). Burning incense belonged to the priests alone (26:18), so these words are meant for the priests among the Levites.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: Readable says "servants" for "ministers", the plainer word for those who serve in the temple.

records.source: וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ הַ֠לְוִיִּם מַ֣חַת בֶּן־עֲמָשַׂ֞י וְיוֹאֵ֣ל בֶּן־עֲזַרְיָהוּ֮ מִן־בְּנֵ֣י הַקְּהָתִי֒ וּמִן־בְּנֵ֣י מְרָרִ֔י קִ֚ישׁ בֶּן־עַבְדִּ֔י וַעֲזַרְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־יְהַלֶּלְאֵ֑ל וּמִן־הַגֵּ֣רְשֻׁנִּ֔י יוֹאָח֙ בֶּן־זִמָּ֔ה וְעֵ֖דֶן בֶּן־יוֹאָֽח׃

decisions.choice: arose: set to work
decisions.reason: "Arise" often means to get up and begin to act (1 Chronicles 22:16).

decisions.choice: the three clans of Levi, then four more families
decisions.reason: The list begins with the three clans descended from Levi's sons Kohath, Merari and Gershon (Numbers 3:17; 1 Chronicles 23:6). Verses 13-14 add the family of Elizaphan, and the families of the three singers Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun. Two men are named from each of the seven groups.

decisions.choice: the men named: leaders of their families in Hezekiah's day
decisions.reason: Several of these names occur in earlier Levite family lists (Mahath, Amasai and Joel in 1 Chronicles 6:20-21; Zimmah and Joah in 6:5-6), since families reused names. The men here are later members of those lines.

decisions.choice: set to work
decisions.reason: Balanced says what their rising meant. Literal keeps "arose".

decisions.choice: the clan of Kohath, of Merari, of Gershon
decisions.reason: Readable names each clan by its ancestor, as 1 Chronicles 15:5 does, and makes each group its own sentence.

decisions.choice: Elizaphan: the head of a leading Kohathite family
decisions.reason: Elizaphan was the leader of the Kohathite clans in the wilderness (Numbers 3:30). By David's time his descendants were counted as a family of their own (1 Chronicles 15:8), and so they are here.

decisions.choice: Jeiel: the name as read aloud
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell the name Jeuel; the vowels and the margin give Jeiel, the reading followed here. Both are forms found among Levite names (1 Chronicles 9:6; 15:18).

decisions.choice: Asaph: the family of one of David's chief singers
decisions.reason: Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun led the music David set up for worship (1 Chronicles 15:17; 25:1). Their descendants formed the singers' families, and they too took part in the cleansing.

decisions.choice: From the family of
decisions.reason: Readable says "family" for "sons" here, since these are smaller family lines inside the clan of Kohath and the singers' guilds, and makes each group its own sentence.

records.source: וַיַּֽאַסְפ֤וּ אֶת־אֲחֵיהֶם֙ וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ כְמִצְוַת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּדִבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לְטַהֵ֖ר בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they gathered their brothers and consecrated themselves and came, according to [the] command of the king, in [the] words of Yahweh, to cleanse [the] house of Yahweh.
pieces: They gathered their relatives and consecrated themselves, and they came to cleanse the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as the king had commanded by the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.15: And they gathered their brothers and consecrated themselves, and they came, according to the command of the king, by the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to cleanse the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.15: They gathered the other Levites, and they all made themselves holy. Then they went in to make the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} clean, as the king had commanded. His command followed the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: their brothers: their fellow Levites
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means the other members of their tribe, whom the fourteen leaders called together for the work.

decisions.choice: by the words of Yahweh: the king's command agreed with what Yahweh had said
alternatives: the king's order was given at Yahweh's word, through a prophet
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means that Hezekiah's order followed the Law, which says the sanctuary must be kept clean and holy. It could also mean that the order itself came through a word from Yahweh, given by a prophet (compare 30:12).

decisions.choice: to cleanse: to make ritually clean
decisions.reason: The verb means to remove whatever makes a person or place unfit for God's presence (Leviticus 16:19). Here it means clearing out everything unclean and making the house fit for worship again.

decisions.choice: relatives (Balanced); the other Levites (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "relatives" for "brothers", as 1 Chronicles 15 does; Readable says who they were.

decisions.choice: His command followed the words of the LORD.
decisions.reason: Readable makes a separate sentence of the phrase, so that the link between the king's order and Yahweh's words is clear.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ הַ֠כֹּהֲנִים לִפְנִ֣ימָה בֵית־יְהוָה֮ לְטַהֵר֒ וַיּוֹצִ֗יאוּ אֵ֤ת כָּל־הַטֻּמְאָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָֽצְאוּ֙ בְּהֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה לַחֲצַ֖ר בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיְקַבְּלוּ֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְהוֹצִ֥יא לְנַֽחַל־קִדְר֖וֹן חֽוּצָה׃

L.16: And the priests went into the inner part of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to cleanse [it], and they brought out all the uncleanness that they found in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the court of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And the Levites received [it] to take [it] out to the Wadi Kidron outside.

R.16: The priests went into the inner rooms of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house to make it clean. They brought everything unclean that they found in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple out into the courtyard of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house. Then the Levites took it and carried it out of the city to the Kidron Valley.

decisions.choice: the priests went inside; the Levites carried things away
decisions.reason: Only the priests could enter the temple building itself (Numbers 18:3, 7). So they brought everything out into the court, and the Levites, who could work in the courts, took it from there.

decisions.choice: the temple: the main building of the house of Yahweh
decisions.reason: This word names the temple building, or its main hall, as distinct from the courts around it.

decisions.choice: the uncleanness: everything that made the place unclean
decisions.reason: The word covers whatever defiled the sanctuary, including idols and objects used in other worship, as in verse 5.

decisions.choice: the Wadi Kidron: the valley east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Kidron lies between the city and the Mount of Olives. Its streambed was dry for most of the year. Asa had burned Maacah's idol there (15:16), and Josiah would do the same with the objects of Baal worship (2 Kings 23:4, 6; compare 2 Chronicles 30:14).

decisions.choice: out of the city
decisions.reason: Readable says what "outside" means: outside the city, where the Kidron Valley lies.

Then for eight days they consecrated the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.

L.17: And they began on the first [day] of the first month to consecrate, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the porch of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and they consecrated the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.

R.17: They started this work on the first day of the first month. By the eighth day of the month they had reached the porch of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. Then they spent eight more days making {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house holy, and they finished on the sixteenth day of the first month.

decisions.choice: the work moved from the courts inward
decisions.reason: For the first eight days they worked in the courts until they reached the porch at the front of the temple. In the next eight days they made the temple building itself holy.

decisions.choice: the sixteenth day: two days past the Passover
decisions.reason: The Passover was to be kept on the fourteenth day of the first month (Exodus 12:6). Because the cleansing was not finished until the sixteenth, the Passover was kept a month later (30:2-3, 15).

decisions.choice: eight more days
decisions.reason: Readable says "more" so that the second eight days are not read as the same eight days as before.

decisions.choice: went inside: into the palace, to the king
decisions.reason: "Inside" here means into the royal palace where the king was.

decisions.choice: the altar of burnt offering: the great bronze altar in the court
decisions.reason: This is the altar Solomon made, where the daily offerings were burned (4:1; 7:7).

decisions.choice: the table of the rows: the table for the bread set before Yahweh
decisions.reason: Twelve loaves were set in two rows on a table in the holy place each Sabbath (Leviticus 24:5-9; 2 Chronicles 13:11).

decisions.choice: the rows of bread (Balanced); the holy bread set out in rows (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was set out in rows, which the Hebrew leaves to the reader to know.

decisions.choice: discarded: rejected and put out of use
decisions.reason: The verb means to reject or cast off. Ahaz treated the utensils of the temple as worthless and put them aside.

decisions.choice: what Ahaz did in his unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: Ahaz cut up the utensils of the house of God and shut its doors (28:24), and he took apart the bronze stands and basin and moved the bronze altar to make room for an altar copied from Damascus (2 Kings 16:10-17). "Unfaithfulness" is the word of verse 6.

decisions.choice: what Ahaz did first, then what the Levites did
decisions.reason: Readable tells what Ahaz did before what the Levites did, in separate sentences.

decisions.choice: rose early: acted at once and with eagerness

decisions.choice: the princes of the city: the leading men of Jerusalem

decisions.choice: the next morning

records.source: וַיָּבִ֣יאוּ פָרִים־שִׁבְעָה֩ וְאֵילִ֨ים שִׁבְעָ֜ה וּכְבָשִׂ֣ים שִׁבְעָ֗ה וּצְפִירֵ֨י עִזִּ֤ים שִׁבְעָה֙ לְחַטָּ֔את עַל־הַמַּמְלָכָ֥ה וְעַל־הַמִּקְדָּ֖שׁ וְעַל־יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לִבְנֵ֤י אַהֲרֹן֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים לְהַעֲל֖וֹת עַל־מִזְבַּ֥ח יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they brought bulls seven and rams seven and lambs seven and he-goats of [the] goats seven, for a sin offering for the kingdom and for the sanctuary and for Judah; and he said to [the] sons of Aaron, the priests, to offer up on [the] altar of Yahweh.
pieces: Seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs and seven male goats were brought as a sin offering on behalf of the kingdom, the sanctuary and Judah. The king told the priests, Aaron's descendants, to offer them up on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s altar.

L.21: And they brought seven bulls and seven rams and seven lambs and seven male goats, for a sin offering for the kingdom and for the sanctuary and for Judah. And he told the sons of Aaron, the priests, to offer [them] up on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: Seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs and seven male goats were brought to be a sin offering for the kingdom, for the temple and for the people of Judah. The king told the priests, Aaron's descendants, to offer them on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s altar.

decisions.choice: as a sin offering: the purpose of the whole group, though only the goats were sin offerings in the strict sense
alternatives: all twenty-eight animals were sin offerings
decisions.reason: Verse 22 deals with the bulls, rams and lambs as burnt offerings are dealt with, and verses 23-24 treat the goats as the sin offering, with the king saying the burnt offering and the sin offering were for all Israel. So the phrase most likely states what the whole set of offerings was for, to deal with sin, while the goats alone were sin offerings. Some take all twenty-eight animals as sin offerings.

decisions.choice: seven of each: a full and complete offering
decisions.reason: Seven is the number of completeness. The Law asked for one bull when the whole community sinned (Leviticus 4:13-21); this offering goes far beyond it.

decisions.choice: the kingdom, the sanctuary and Judah: the king's house, the temple and the people
decisions.reason: "The kingdom" most likely means the king and the royal house, which had led the people astray under Ahaz; "the sanctuary" is the temple and its priests; "Judah" is the people. Every part of the nation needed cleansing.

decisions.choice: the sons of Aaron, the priests: only priests could serve at the altar
decisions.reason: The Law gave the work of the altar to Aaron's descendants alone (Numbers 18:7; 1 Chronicles 6:34).

decisions.choice: The king
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, since "they" brought the animals but "he" gave the order.

decisions.choice: the temple; the people of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for "sanctuary" and "the people of Judah" for "Judah".

records.source: וַֽיִּשְׁחֲטוּ֙ הַבָּקָ֔ר וַיְקַבְּל֤וּ הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֶת־הַדָּ֔ם וַֽיִּזְרְק֖וּ הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חָה וַיִּשְׁחֲט֣וּ הָאֵלִ֗ים וַיִּזְרְק֤וּ הַדָּם֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה וַֽיִּשְׁחֲטוּ֙ הַכְּבָשִׂ֔ים וַיִּזְרְק֥וּ הַדָּ֖ם הַמִּזְבֵּֽחָה׃
records.gloss: And they slaughtered the cattle, and received the priests the blood and threw [it] at the altar; and they slaughtered the rams and threw the blood at the altar; and they slaughtered the lambs and threw the blood at the altar.
pieces: So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests received the blood and splashed it against the altar. Next they slaughtered the rams and splashed their blood against the altar, and then they slaughtered the lambs and splashed their blood against the altar.

L.22: And they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests received the blood and threw [it] against the altar. And they slaughtered the rams and threw the blood against the altar. And they slaughtered the lambs and threw the blood against the altar.

R.22: They killed the bulls, and the priests caught the blood and splashed it against the altar. Then they killed the rams and splashed their blood against the altar. Then they killed the lambs and splashed their blood against the altar.

decisions.choice: threw the blood against the altar: splashed it
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw or dash a liquid, as in the rite of the burnt offering (Leviticus 1:5, 11).

decisions.choice: they slaughtered: the slaughterers are not named
decisions.reason: "They" may be the priests, as in verse 24, or the Levites, who helped the priests when there were too few (verse 34).

decisions.choice: the bulls, rams and lambs: treated as burnt offerings
decisions.reason: The steps, slaughtering and splashing the blood against the altar, are those of the burnt offering. See the note at verse 21.

decisions.choice: the bulls
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has a word for cattle in general, but it refers back to the bulls of verse 21.

records.source: וַיַּגִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ אֶת־שְׂעִירֵ֣י הַֽחַטָּ֔את לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְהַקָּהָ֑ל וַיִּסְמְכ֥וּ יְדֵיהֶ֖ם עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they brought near [the] goats of the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.
pieces: Then the goats for the sin offering were brought before the king and the assembly, and these laid their hands on them.

L.23: And they brought the goats of the sin offering near before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.

R.23: Then they brought the goats for the sin offering to the king and the people gathered there, and the king and the people put their hands on the goats.

decisions.choice: laid their hands on them: claimed the offering as their own
decisions.reason: Laying hands on the animal showed that it was offered for those who laid them, and that it stood in their place (Leviticus 1:4; 4:15; 16:21).

decisions.choice: they laid: the king and the assembly
alternatives: the priests, on behalf of the king and assembly
decisions.reason: Those who laid hands on the goats were most likely the king and the assembly, before whom the goats were brought, as the elders did for the whole community (Leviticus 4:15). The verb has no named subject, so it could also be the priests acting for them.

decisions.choice: goats: the same animals as the male goats of verse 21
decisions.reason: A different word for a male goat is used here, the usual word for the goat of a sin offering (Leviticus 4:23; 16:9).

decisions.choice: and these laid (Balanced); the king and the people (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who laid on their hands, following meaning note 2. Literal keeps the bare "they".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁחָטוּם֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וַֽיְחַטְּא֤וּ אֶת־דָּמָם֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה לְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י לְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הָעוֹלָ֖ה וְהַחַטָּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And slaughtered them the priests and made a sin offering [with] their blood on the altar to make atonement for all Israel, for for all Israel said the king the burnt offering and the sin offering.
pieces: The priests slaughtered the goats and applied their blood to the altar as a sin offering, making atonement for all Israel. The king had said that the burnt offering and the sin offering were to be for all Israel.

L.24: And the priests slaughtered them and made a sin offering with their blood on the altar, to make atonement for all Israel, for the king had said, for all Israel the burnt offering and the sin offering.

R.24: The priests killed the goats and put their blood on the altar as a sin offering. This was to make atonement for all Israel, because the king had ordered that the burnt offering and the sin offering be made for all Israel.

decisions.choice: made a sin offering with their blood: cleansed the altar with the blood
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the same root as "sin offering". It means to remove sin and its defilement, here by putting the blood on the altar (Leviticus 8:15).

decisions.choice: to make atonement: to cover sin and cleanse from it
decisions.reason: Atonement here means removing the guilt and defilement that stood between Yahweh and his people, so that he could again dwell among them (Leviticus 4:20; 16:16).

decisions.choice: for all Israel: the whole people, not Judah only
decisions.reason: Verse 21 spoke of Judah, but the king widens the offering to "all Israel", the north as well. Hezekiah will go on to invite the northern tribes to his Passover (30:1, 5-6). The Hebrew puts "for all Israel" first in the king's words for emphasis.

decisions.choice: The king had said ... were to be for all Israel
decisions.reason: "Said" here means gave an order, as often in Chronicles. Balanced keeps "said" and makes the clause its own sentence; Readable says "ordered". Literal keeps "said".

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲמֵ֨ד אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֜ם בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֗ה בִּמְצִלְתַּ֨יִם֙ בִּנְבָלִ֣ים וּבְכִנֹּר֔וֹת בְּמִצְוַ֥ת דָּוִ֛יד וְגָ֥ד חֹזֵֽה־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְנָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֑יא כִּ֧י בְיַד־יְהוָ֛ה הַמִּצְוָ֖ה בְּיַד־נְבִיאָֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: And he stationed the Levites [in the] house of Yahweh with cymbals, with harps and with lyres, according to [the] command of David and Gad, [the] seer of the king, and Nathan the prophet; for by [the] hand of Yahweh [was] the command, by [the] hand of his prophets.
pieces: He placed the Levites in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house with cymbals, harps and lyres, as David had commanded, together with Gad the king's seer and Nathan the prophet. The command had come from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets.

L.25: And he stationed the Levites in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with cymbals, with harps and with lyres, according to the command of David and of Gad the king's seer and of Nathan the prophet; for the command [was] by the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, by the hand of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets.

R.25: Hezekiah placed the Levites in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple with cymbals, harps and lyres. He did what David had commanded, and Gad and Nathan too. Gad was the king's seer, a prophet who brought the king messages from God, and Nathan was a prophet. The command had come from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets.

decisions.choice: the command of David, Gad and Nathan: the order of worship set up under David
decisions.reason: David appointed the Levites to sing and play before the ark and later in the temple (1 Chronicles 15:16-24; 16:4-6; 25:1-7). Gad and Nathan were the prophets of David's court (1 Chronicles 17:1-2; 21:9; 29:29). Only here are they said to have shared in ordering the temple music.

decisions.choice: seer: a prophet to whom God gave visions
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to see". It is another title for a prophet, as Gad is called both (1 Chronicles 21:9; 29:29).

decisions.choice: by the hand of: through
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means by means of someone. The command came from Yahweh, and his prophets were the ones through whom it came.

decisions.choice: the command was from Yahweh: the music had divine authority
decisions.reason: Chronicles stresses that the singing in the temple was not only David's idea. It was ordered by Yahweh, as the plan of the temple itself was (1 Chronicles 28:19).

decisions.choice: harps; lyres
decisions.reason: The names kept for these two stringed instruments, as in 2 Chronicles 5:12.

decisions.choice: a prophet who brought the king messages from God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "seer" the first time it comes in the chapter, as 1 Chronicles 21:9 does.

records.source: וַיַּֽעַמְד֤וּ הַלְוִיִּם֙ בִּכְלֵ֣י דָוִ֔יד וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים בַּחֲצֹצְרֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: And stood the Levites with [the] instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.
pieces: The Levites stood ready with David's instruments, and the priests with the trumpets.

L.26: And the Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.

R.26: The Levites stood ready with the instruments that David had made, and the priests stood with their trumpets.

decisions.choice: the instruments of David: those David had made for worship
decisions.reason: David had instruments made for praising Yahweh (1 Chronicles 23:5; 2 Chronicles 7:6).

decisions.choice: the priests with the trumpets
decisions.reason: The trumpets were blown by the priests (Numbers 10:8; 1 Chronicles 15:24; 16:6).

decisions.choice: stood ready; that David had made
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "stood ready", since they were waiting to begin (verse 27). Readable explains "David's instruments" from 1 Chronicles 23:5.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ לְהַעֲל֥וֹת הָעֹלָ֖ה לְהַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וּבְעֵ֞ת הֵחֵ֣ל הָֽעוֹלָ֗ה הֵחֵ֤ל שִׁיר־יְהוָה֙ וְהַחֲצֹ֣צְר֔וֹת וְעַ֨ל־יְדֵ֔י כְּלֵ֖י דָּוִ֥יד מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said Hezekiah to offer up the burnt offering on the altar; and at [the] time began the burnt offering began [the] song of Yahweh and the trumpets, and on [the] hands of [the] instruments of David king of Israel.
pieces: Then Hezekiah ordered the burnt offering to be offered on the altar. When the burnt offering began, the song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} began too, with the trumpets, accompanied by the instruments of David king of Israel.

L.27: And Hezekiah said to offer up the burnt offering on the altar. And at the time the burnt offering began, the song of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} began, and the trumpets, together with the instruments of David king of Israel.

R.27: Then Hezekiah gave the order to offer the burnt offering on the altar. As the offering began, the Levites began to sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The trumpets sounded, along with the instruments made by David, king of Israel.

decisions.choice: the song of Yahweh: the song sung in his worship
decisions.reason: This is the song of praise to Yahweh that belonged to the temple service (compare Psalm 137:4).

decisions.choice: on the hands of the instruments: together with them, led by them
alternatives: under the direction of the instruments
decisions.reason: The phrase literally speaks of the "hands" of the instruments. It most likely means that the instruments played along with the song and the trumpets. It may instead mean that the song was guided by them, as the singers were "under the hands of" their leaders (1 Chronicles 25:2).

decisions.choice: the song began when the burnt offering began
decisions.reason: Praise and sacrifice went together: the singing lasted as long as the offering was burning (verse 28; 1 Chronicles 16:40-42).

decisions.choice: ordered (Balanced); gave the order (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Said" here means gave an order, as in verse 24.

decisions.choice: the Levites began to sing
decisions.reason: Readable names the singers, who were the Levites (verse 25).

records.source: וְכָל־הַקָּהָל֙ מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִ֔ים וְהַשִּׁ֣יר מְשׁוֹרֵ֔ר וְהַחֲצֹצְר֖וֹת מַחְצְרִ֑יםהַכֹּ֕ל עַ֖ד לִכְל֥וֹת הָעֹלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And all the assembly [were] bowing down, and the song [was] singing and the trumpets [were] sounding; all [of it] until [the] finishing of the burnt offering.
pieces: The whole assembly bowed down in worship while the singers sang and the trumpeters sounded the trumpets. All this went on until the burnt offering was finished.

L.28: And all the assembly was bowing down, and the song was singing, and the trumpets were sounding; all [this] until the burnt offering was finished.

R.28: All the people bowed down to worship while the singers sang and the trumpets were blown. This went on until the burnt offering was finished.

decisions.choice: bowing down: worshiping with the body
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low, often to the ground, and is the usual word for worship.

decisions.choice: the song was singing, the trumpets were sounding: the singers and the trumpeters
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the song and the trumpets as if they did the singing and the sounding. It means the people who sang and played.

decisions.choice: sounding: the written form and the form read aloud differ slightly
decisions.reason: The written consonants and the vowels give two spellings of the verb for blowing a trumpet. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the singers sang and the trumpeters sounded the trumpets
decisions.reason: Balanced names the people meant (meaning note 2). Readable says "the trumpets were blown".

records.source: וּכְכַלּ֖וֹת לְהַעֲל֑וֹת כָּרְע֗וּ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָֽל־הַנִּמְצְאִ֥ים אִתּ֖וֹ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And when finished to offer up, bowed the king and all the ones found with him, and worshiped.
pieces: When the offering was finished, the king and everyone present with him knelt down and worshiped.

L.29: And when they had finished offering [it] up, the king and all who were present with him knelt and worshiped.

R.29: When they had finished offering the sacrifice, the king and everyone there with him knelt down and worshiped.

decisions.choice: knelt: bent the knee
decisions.reason: The verb means to bend the knees, to kneel low.

decisions.choice: worshiped: bowed down in worship
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 28: to bow low before Yahweh.

decisions.choice: all who were found with him: everyone present
decisions.reason: "Those found" with someone means those who were there at the time.

decisions.choice: knelt down
decisions.reason: "Knelt" keeps the sense of bending the knee, and is different from the bowing of verse 28.

records.source: וַ֠יֹּאמֶר יְחִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִים֙ לַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְהַלֵּל֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה בְּדִבְרֵ֥י דָוִ֖יד וְאָסָ֣ף הַחֹזֶ֑ה וַֽיְהַלְלוּ֙ עַד־לְשִׂמְחָ֔ה וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֽוּ׃פ
records.gloss: And said Hezekiah the king and the princes to the Levites to praise Yahweh with [the] words of David and Asaph the seer; and they praised to joy, and bowed down and worshiped.
pieces: King Hezekiah and the officials told the Levites to praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} using the words of David and of Asaph the seer. They praised joyfully, and they bowed their heads and worshiped.

L.30: And Hezekiah the king and the princes told the Levites to praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with the words of David and of Asaph the seer. And they praised with joy, and they bowed and worshiped.

R.30: King Hezekiah and the leaders told the Levites to praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with the songs written by David and by Asaph the seer. So the Levites sang praises with great joy. Then they bowed down and worshiped.

decisions.choice: the words of David and Asaph: their psalms
decisions.reason: Many psalms carry the names of David or Asaph (Psalms 50; 73-83). The first song given to Asaph and his relatives is in 1 Chronicles 16:7-36.

decisions.choice: Asaph the seer: a singer who also spoke from God
decisions.reason: The singers are said to have prophesied with their instruments (1 Chronicles 25:1-2), and Asaph's psalms often speak as messages from God (Psalm 50; 81). So he too is called a seer, as in verse 25.

decisions.choice: to joy: with great joy
decisions.reason: "Until joy" means that the praise rose to great gladness.

decisions.choice: bowed: bowed the head
decisions.reason: This verb is used for bowing the head, often together with the verb for bowing to the ground in worship (Exodus 4:31).

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the songs written by
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the words of David and Asaph" are.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַן יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר עַתָּ֨ה מִלֵּאתֶ֤ם יֶדְכֶם֙ לַיהוָ֔ה גֹּ֧שׁוּ וְהָבִ֛יאוּ זְבָחִ֥ים וְתוֹד֖וֹת לְבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּבִ֤יאוּ הַקָּהָל֙ זְבָחִ֣ים וְתוֹד֔וֹת וְכָל־נְדִ֥יב לֵ֖ב עֹלֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And answered Hezekiah and said, now you have filled your hand to Yahweh; come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to [the] house of Yahweh. And brought the assembly sacrifices and thank offerings, and every willing of heart burnt offerings.
pieces: Then Hezekiah said, "Now you have dedicated yourselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Come near; bring sacrifices and thank offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house." The assembly brought their sacrifices and thank offerings, and all who were willing at heart brought burnt offerings.

L.31: And Hezekiah answered and said, "Now you have filled your hand for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." And the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and every one willing of heart [brought] burnt offerings.

R.31: Then Hezekiah said, "Now you have given yourselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Come and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple." So the people brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and everyone who wanted to also brought burnt offerings.

decisions.choice: you have filled your hand: you have dedicated yourselves
alternatives: spoken to the priests: you are now installed for Yahweh's service
decisions.reason: "Filling the hand" is the phrase for installing priests in their office (Exodus 28:41), and it is also used of the people giving themselves to Yahweh's service (1 Chronicles 29:5). Since the assembly answers by bringing offerings, Hezekiah is most likely speaking to the whole assembly, now that the house is clean and atonement has been made. He could instead be speaking to the priests, whose consecration is complete.

decisions.choice: sacrifices and thank offerings: offerings shared in a meal
decisions.reason: "Sacrifices" here are the offerings whose meat the worshipers ate before Yahweh, and the thank offering was one kind of them, given to thank God (Leviticus 7:11-15). A burnt offering, by contrast, was burned whole.

decisions.choice: every one willing of heart: all who chose to give freely
decisions.reason: A "willing heart" gives of its own accord, without being required (Exodus 35:5, 22). These burnt offerings were freewill offerings.

decisions.choice: answered: began to speak
decisions.reason: "Answered and said" often begins a speech that responds to the situation, not to a question.

decisions.choice: dedicated yourselves (Balanced); given yourselves (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom; Literal keeps "filled your hand". The words for ordaining priests are not used, since the speech is most likely to the people.

records.source: וַיְהִ֞י מִסְפַּ֣ר הָעֹלָה֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵבִ֣יאוּ הַקָּהָל֒ בָּקָ֣ר שִׁבְעִ֔ים אֵילִ֥ים מֵאָ֖ה כְּבָשִׂ֣ים מָאתָ֑יִם לְעֹלָ֥ה לַיהוָ֖ה כָּל־אֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And was [the] number of the burnt offering that brought the assembly: cattle seventy, rams a hundred, lambs two hundred; for a burnt offering to Yahweh [were] all these.
pieces: The number of burnt offerings that the assembly brought was seventy bulls, 100 rams and 200 lambs. All these were for burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.32: And the number of the burnt offerings that the assembly brought was: seventy bulls, 100 rams, 200 lambs; all these [were] for a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.32: The people brought seventy bulls, 100 rams and 200 lambs. All of these were offered to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as burnt offerings.

decisions.choice: the burnt offerings: gifts burned whole
decisions.reason: These are the freewill burnt offerings of verse 31. Nothing of them was eaten; all of it was given to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: bulls
decisions.reason: The word for cattle refers to bulls here, as in verse 22. The numbers follow the rule of words up to ninety-nine and numerals above.

records.source: וְֽהַקֳּדָשִׁ֑ים בָּקָר֙ שֵׁ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת וְצֹ֖אן שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִֽים׃
records.gloss: And the holy things: cattle six hundred and sheep three thousand.
pieces: The consecrated offerings were 600 bulls and 3,000 sheep.

L.33: And the holy things [were] 600 bulls and 3,000 sheep.

R.33: The other offerings set apart for God were 600 bulls and 3,000 sheep.

decisions.choice: the holy things: the offerings that were shared in a meal
decisions.reason: "Holy things" here are the sacrifices and thank offerings of verse 31, as distinct from the burnt offerings counted in verse 32. Part of them was burned on the altar, and the rest was eaten by the worshipers and priests (compare 35:13).

decisions.choice: sheep: animals from the flock
decisions.reason: The word means a flock of small animals and can include goats.

decisions.choice: consecrated offerings (Balanced); the other offerings set apart for God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced says what kind of holy things are meant. Readable explains "consecrated" and sets them beside the burnt offerings of verse 32.

records.source: רַ֤ק הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ הָי֣וּ לִמְעָ֔ט וְלֹ֣א יָֽכְל֔וּ לְהַפְשִׁ֖יט אֶת־כָּל־הָעֹל֑וֹת וַֽיְּחַזְּק֞וּם אֲחֵיהֶ֣ם הַלְוִיִּ֗ם עַד־כְּל֤וֹת הַמְּלָאכָה֙ וְעַ֣ד יִתְקַדְּשׁ֣וּ הַכֹּֽהֲנִ֔ים כִּ֤י הַלְוִיִּם֙ יִשְׁרֵ֣י לֵבָ֔ב לְהִתְקַדֵּ֖שׁ מֵֽהַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃
records.gloss: Only the priests were to fewness, and not they were able to skin all the burnt offerings; and helped them their brothers the Levites until [the] finishing of the work and until consecrated themselves the priests, for the Levites [were] more upright of heart to consecrate themselves than the priests.
pieces: But the priests were too few to skin all the burnt offerings. So their relatives the Levites helped them until the task was done and the priests had consecrated themselves, for the Levites were more upright in heart to consecrate themselves than the priests.

L.34: But the priests were too few, and they were not able to skin all the burnt offerings; so their brothers the Levites helped them until the work was finished and until the priests had consecrated themselves, for the Levites [were] more upright of heart to consecrate themselves than the priests.

R.34: But there were not enough priests to skin all the animals for the burnt offerings. So their relatives the Levites helped them until the work was done and until more priests had made themselves holy. The Levites had been more careful than the priests to make themselves holy.

decisions.choice: to skin the burnt offerings
decisions.reason: The hide of a burnt offering was removed before it was cut up and burned (Leviticus 1:6). With so many animals, and few priests ready, the Levites were needed to help (compare 35:11).

decisions.choice: more upright of heart: more earnest and conscientious
decisions.reason: An "upright heart" is one that is honest and set on doing what is right (Psalm 7:11; 32:11). The Levites had been quicker and more careful to make themselves ready than many of the priests.

decisions.choice: until the priests had consecrated themselves: until more priests were ready
decisions.reason: Not enough priests had yet made themselves holy for the work, and the same shortage held up the Passover (30:3). The Levites helped until enough priests were ready.

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

decisions.choice: more priests; more careful
decisions.reason: Readable says "more priests" to make clear that some priests were not yet ready (meaning note 3), and "more careful" for "more upright of heart".

records.source: וְגַם־עֹלָ֨ה לָרֹ֜ב בְּחֶלְבֵ֧י הַשְּׁלָמִ֛ים וּבַנְּסָכִ֖ים לָעֹלָ֑ה וַתִּכּ֖וֹן עֲבוֹדַ֥ת בֵּית־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And also burnt offering [was] in abundance, with [the] fat of the peace offerings and with the drink offerings for the burnt offering. And was established [the] service of [the] house of Yahweh.
pieces: Burnt offerings were also plentiful, together with the fat of the peace offerings and the drink offerings that went with each burnt offering. In this way the service of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house was set in order.

L.35: And also burnt offering [was] in abundance, with the fat of the peace offerings and with the drink offerings for the burnt offering. And the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was established.

R.35: There were also many burnt offerings, as well as the fat from the peace offerings and the drink offerings that were poured out with the burnt offerings. So the worship in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple was set up again.

decisions.choice: the fat of the peace offerings and the drink offerings
decisions.reason: The fat of every peace offering was burned on the altar (Leviticus 3:3-5), and each burnt offering was to have its offering of wine poured out (Numbers 15:1-10). All of this added to the priests' work.

decisions.choice: was established: was set in order and made firm
decisions.reason: The verb means to be made ready and firm. After years of neglect, the regular service of the temple was working again (compare 8:16).

decisions.choice: the service: the worship and work of the temple
decisions.reason: The word covers the whole of the work done in Yahweh's house: the offerings, the music and the care of the place.

decisions.choice: set up again
decisions.reason: Readable says "again", since the service had stopped under Ahaz (verse 7).

records.gloss: And rejoiced Hezekiah and all the people over that had prepared God for the people, for in suddenness was the thing.
pieces: Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced over what God had prepared for the people, for the thing had come about suddenly.

L.36: And Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced over what God had prepared for the people, for the thing had come about suddenly.

R.36: Hezekiah and all the people were glad about what God had done for them, because it had all happened so quickly.

decisions.choice: what God had prepared: the article used as "what"
alternatives: because God had made the people ready
decisions.reason: The article stands before the verb here in the sense "that which". God is the one who had made things ready for the people. Some read it as "because God had made the people ready".

decisions.choice: suddenly: quickly and unexpectedly
decisions.reason: The word means suddenly or without warning. The temple, shut for years, was cleansed and its worship restored within sixteen days (verse 17).

decisions.choice: they rejoiced over what God had done
decisions.reason: Chronicles sees the speed of the change as God's work, not only the king's, and joy is its mark of worship that pleases him (30:21, 26).

decisions.choice: what God had done for them; so quickly
decisions.reason: Readable says "done" for "prepared" and "so quickly" for "suddenly".
